title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter VIII 'Analysis situs' (1986) develops a combinatorial formalism for stratified or cell-like decompositions. A set P is covered by subsets |X| indexed by an ordered set of 'pieces' X̃. Each piece has an 'open part' |X|° = |X| minus the union of the |Y| for Y<X.

The page first finishes an argument begun on p.35. Suppose |Y|° is nonempty, the open parts are pairwise disjoint, and each |Z| is the union of the |W|° for W ≤ Z (condition 'ii ter'). Then for x in |Y|°, Y is the smallest element of X̃ such that x ∈ |Z|. Proof: if x ∈ |Z|, then x ∈ |W|° for some W ≤ Z. Disjointness forces W = Y, hence Y ≤ Z.

Grothendieck then remarks that he has been using the relation ≤ without having established its properties (transitivity, its relation to inclusion). He decides to isolate an abstract lemma.

Lemma (stated, proof not written). Data:
- an ordered set I, a set P, and a map φ: I → 𝔓(P), i ↦ X_i;
- the open parts X_i° := X_i \ ⋃_{j<i} X_j.
Hypotheses:
- (i) φ is increasing: i ≤ j ⇒ X_i ⊂ X_j;
- (ii) X_i° ∩ X_j° = ∅ for i ≠ j, and every X_i° ≠ ∅. The first draft 'i ≠ j ⇔ X_i°∩X_j° = ∅' packs both conditions together; together they make φ injective.
Equivalent conditions:
- (iii) the image I' = φ(I) ⊂ 𝔓(P) is a family of the expected kind, described in terms of the I_{≤i} / I_{<i} (partly illegible);
- (iii bis) for every i, X_i = ⋃_{j≤i} X_j°.
Conclusion: these conditions imply φ is an order isomorphism from I onto its image, ordered by inclusion.

Proof of the conclusion (easy). If X_i ⊂ X_j, pick x ∈ X_i° (nonempty). Then x ∈ X_j = ⋃_{k≤j} X_k°, so x ∈ X_k° for some k ≤ j. Disjointness gives k = i, so i ≤ j. The converse is (i).

This is the poset-indexed ('indicial') bookkeeping for stratifications satisfying a frontier-type condition: each 'closed stratum' is the disjoint union of the open strata below it. The next page restates it as a cleaner Proposition with four equivalent conditions, the key one being that each I^x = {i : x ∈ X_i} has a least element.
errors: The first version of (ii), 'i ≠ j ⇔ X_i°∩X_j°=∅', is replaced by the one-way implication plus a separate nonemptiness condition. The biconditional is equivalent only if one reads the i = j case as nonemptiness; the correction is sound.
The lemma is stated without proof, and the content of condition (iii) is unfinished or illegible. This is a draft gap, not a mathematical error.

Implicitly, (iii bis) does not follow from (i)+(ii) when I has infinite descending chains. Example: a decreasing nested family indexed by the negative integers whose intersection is nonempty; points of the intersection lie in no X_j°. This is consistent with the next page's remark 'automat. si I fini'.

ideas.what: Open strata X_i° = X_i minus the union of the X_j for j<i attached to a poset-indexed increasing family of subsets; requiring them nonempty and pairwise disjoint
ideas.modern_name: poset-indexed stratification / decomposition of a set into strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (stratifications); the poset-stratified formalism in Lurie (Higher Algebra, appendix A) and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses 'tame topology' and stratified structures informally; this combinatorial lemma is not known to appear there

ideas.what: Frontier-type condition X_i = union of X_j° for j ≤ i, implying that the index order coincides with inclusion of closed strata (order isomorphism I → φ(I))
ideas.modern_name: frontier condition; the poset of strata ordered by closure-inclusion; equivalently a map to the poset with its Alexandrov topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in stratification theory (Whitney, Mather) and in the combinatorics of CW / regular cell complexes

ideas.what: Each point x has a smallest index i with x ∈ X_i, namely the unique i with x ∈ X_i°
ideas.modern_name: the 'stratum map' P → I sending a point to its stratum index (continuous for the Alexandrov topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; made explicit in modern poset-stratified spaces (Lurie, Higher Algebra A.5)

deep.surprise_reason: This is correct, elementary bookkeeping: a poset-indexed family of subsets whose open parts partition the space and satisfy the frontier condition, so the index order equals inclusion. It is standard in stratification theory and is a draft of the proposition on the next page. There is no new result or unexploited connection beyond the general historical interest of Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' formalism.
transcription_corrections: 'par disjonction[?] Y ∈ Z̃ donc Y ≤ Z' — probably 'par définition' or 'par disjonction des |W|°'. The argument is: x ∈ |Z| = ⋃_{W∈Z̃}|W|°, so x ∈ |W|° with W ∈ Z̃, and disjointness forces W = Y, so Y ∈ Z̃.

The line 'Dans tous les cas, la relation ≤ n'a pas[?] ... transitive dans l'ensemble ordonné I' likely reads roughly: 'Dans tous les cas, la relation ≤ n'a pas [encore été prouvée] transitive [i.e. qu'on a bien une relation d'ordre]…, donc il faut expliciter le lemme'.

In the lemma, the first statement of (ii) is 'i ≠ j ⇔ X_i°∩X_j° = ∅'. It is corrected to '∀ i,j, i≠j ⇒ X_i°∩X_j°=∅', followed by 'puis la décomposition: ∀i X_i° ≠ ∅' and the parenthetical '(…et φ est injective)'.
'(iii) φ(I) = I' ⊂ 𝔓(P) est une famille …' — the marginal insertion reads 'I_{≤i} ou I_{<i}'. The rest of (iii) is largely illegible.
